Competitive Analysis

Market Insights

🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Understand the Content Collapse and why 80% of content is becoming invisible
  • Distinguish performative vs genuine thought leadership
  • Apply the Three-Layer Content Operating Model
  • Optimize content for GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)

The 80/20 Pattern

We read every AI + PMM article from a daily digest for an entire month. 35 editions. 180 articles. The pattern was stark:

80%
Competent and interchangeable. Could have been written by any of a hundred people — or by no person at all.

❌ The 80% (Generic)

  • Solid writing, reasonable arguments
  • Nothing memorable 20 minutes later
  • "5 Things Every CMO Needs to Know"
  • Same frameworks with different metaphors
  • Total information content: approximately zero

✅ The 20% (Differentiated)

  • Specific experience from real work
  • Contrarian takes backed by evidence
  • Stories nobody else can tell
  • Technical depth that can't be faked
  • Voice that's recognizably human

The Ratio Is About to Get Worse

The 80% that's competent and interchangeable is exactly the content that AI produces most easily. And the marginal cost of producing it is dropping toward zero. When everyone can generate "good enough" content instantly, only the genuinely differentiated 20% breaks through.

The Content Collapse

In 2023, a competent PMM produced maybe 15,000 words of original content per month — blog posts, social, quarterly thought pieces. That represented a significant chunk of working time.

In 2026, that same PMM with Claude or ChatGPT can produce that volume in a day. Not at the same quality, maybe. But at a quality level that's indistinguishable from human-written content to most readers.

The supply of competent marketing content is exploding while the demand — the finite attention of your buyers — stays the same.

Performative vs Genuine

💀 Performative Thought Leadership (Dying)

  • Performs appearance of insight without delivering
  • Listicles and framework-of-the-week
  • AI produces it at scale
  • Readers developing antibodies to it

🌟 Genuine Thought Leadership (Scarce)

  • Done something, seen something, learned something
  • Specific point of view, grounded in experience
  • Voice that's recognizably human
  • The only kind that matters now

The Narrative Advantage

AI can generate a competent analogy. It can produce a hypothetical scenario. But it can't tell you about the Porsche on the tarmac at the Atlanta airport, because it wasn't there.

💡 Stories That Stick

Consider identity resolution — the technical process of matching customer records across systems. You could explain deterministic vs probabilistic matching. Or you could tell the story of the Porsche sitting on the tarmac at the Atlanta airport — a Delta SkyMiles play where they knew exactly which high-value customers to surprise with an upgrade experience.

The technical explanation would put you to sleep. The Porsche on the runway wakes you up.

What AI Can't Replicate

The specificity of lived experience — the named person, the exact question, the energy in the room — is the thing that makes a story stick. The PMM who has real stories from real customer conversations, real deal cycles, real product failures and recoveries, has something no AI agent can replicate. Not because the technology isn't good enough. Because the stories require having been somewhere and paid attention.

GEO: The Agent as Reader

When a buyer asks ChatGPT or Claude or Perplexity to recommend vendors for a specific use case, the AI synthesizes from the content it can access — web pages, documentation, analyst reports, blog posts.

❌ Invisible to GEO

"Unlocking the Power of Data-Driven Insights"

Too vague to be cited for any concrete buyer question

✅ Agent-Surfaceable

"How We Reduced Supply Chain Forecasting Errors by 34% Using Real-Time ERP Data"

Exactly what AI surfaces for supply chain analytics queries

The same principles that make positioning agent-readable — specificity, structured claims, verifiable evidence — also make content more likely to be surfaced by AI systems.

If your content is generic or vague or behind a registration wall, you don't get cited. In a world where vendor discovery happens through AI search, invisible to the agent means invisible to the buyer.

The Three-Layer Content Operating Model

The time allocation between these layers is roughly the inverse of what most PMM teams practice today:

20%
of time

Layer 1: Commodity Content

Blog posts, social updates, email sequences, slide decks, one-pagers. Should be almost entirely agent-produced. An agent can produce a LinkedIn post 90% as good in 2% of the time. The human reviews, ensures accuracy, adds personality if needed.

👤 Human role: Review & approve
40%
of time

Layer 2: Strategic Content

Pieces that advance positioning and establish POV. GEO investment lives here: deeply specific articles about capabilities, use cases, architecture, customer outcomes. Also competitive content.

👤 Human role: Direct strategy, provide stories, ensure positioning. Agent handles research & drafts.
40%
of time

Layer 3: Signature Content

Conference keynotes, long-form essays, genuinely original frameworks, customer stories with enough texture to feel the room. What makes readers follow you rather than your brand.

👤 Human role: Entirely human. No agent assistance in writing — the point is that it's irreducibly personal.

The Inversion

Most teams today: 60% commodity, 30% strategic, 10% signature.
The 10x move: 20% commodity, 40% strategic, 40% signature.
That transforms content from a production function into a strategic one.

The Practitioner's Playbook

1. Run the GEO Audit

Ask Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity to recommend products in your category for 3-5 specific use cases. Do you show up? Are you cited? Is the info accurate? If invisible or misrepresented, that's a content gap with pipeline implications.

2. Protect Signature Time

Find content from last year with the most engagement — not just views, but comments, shares, inbound from prospects. That's your signature content. Now ask: how much time does that author have to create more? If "not enough," you've found the problem.

3. Build the Commodity Pipeline

Choose your LLM, define templates, create a prompting workflow that produces channel-specific content at quality level you need. Goal: reduce commodity to a review-and-approve workflow. Hours reclaimed go to strategic and signature.

Key Takeaways

  • 80% of content is becoming invisible — competent-but-generic content that AI produces at scale
  • The Narrative Advantage comes from stories only you can tell — lived experience AI can't replicate
  • GEO matters: AI surfaces specific, structured, authoritative content; vague content is invisible
  • Three-layer model: Commodity (20%, agent-produced), Strategic (40%, human-directed), Signature (40%, entirely human)
  • Shift measurement from volume metrics (posts/month) to influence metrics (analyst citations, deal impact)
